issues.legal_issue: An interim injunction extended only until a specified date does not continue after that date merely because it was not expressly vacated.
material_facts: A civil court initially restrained further action and demolition, then extended the injunction in successive orders until specified dates.
At a later adjournment, the court did not extend the injunction, and no subsequent order extended it or granted a fresh injunction.
The suit was eventually dismissed for default.
issues.conclusion: The injunction was not operative after the last date to which it had been extended.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of an interim order determine its duration; where successive orders extend an injunction only until stated dates, it cannot be treated as continuing after the last such date without a further extension or fresh order. The Court rejected the proposition that an injunction necessarily continues until expressly vacated.

predicates.civil_proceeding_with_interim_injunction: A party in a civil proceeding obtained an interim injunction.
predicates.injunction_extended_only_to_stated_dates: The court's successive orders extended the injunction only until stated dates.
predicates.no_later_extension_or_fresh_injunction: After the last stated date, the court made no order extending the injunction or granting a fresh one.
predicates.interim_injunction_ends_on_last_stated_d: The interim injunction ends on the last date to which the court extended it.

issues.definition: When an interim injunction in a civil proceeding was extended only to stated dates and no later order extended or renewed it, the injunction ends on the last stated date.

issues.legal_issue: A declaration of land acquisition made beyond the statutory time limit, after excluding only the period during which the relevant action or proceeding was stayed by a court, is void.
material_facts: A notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, was published on 20 December 1996, and a declaration under Section 6 was made on 29 November 2000.
The interim injunction was extended only until a date in 1998; it was not extended thereafter.
Even after excluding the period during which the injunction operated, the declaration was made beyond one year from publication of the notification.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was beyond the permitted period and was void and of no effect.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(1), proviso (ii), of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, bars a declaration after one year from publication of the Section 4(1) notification; Explanation 1 excludes from that calculation the period during which an action or proceeding taken pursuant to the notification is stayed by a court. The time limit is mandatory, and a declaration made after it expires is void. The Court treated the Act as expropriatory and applied strict construction, relying on Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Darius Shapur Chenai, which referred to State of M.P. v. Vishnu Prasad Sharma, Khub Chand v. State of Rajasthan, and CCE v. Orient Fabrics (P) Ltd.

predicates.land_acquisition_declaration_case: The proceeding concerns the validity of a declaration acquiring land after publication of an acquisition notification.
predicates.declaration_outside_deadline_after_exclu: The declaration was made beyond the applicable time limit even after excluding the period during which a court actually stayed the relevant action or proceeding.
predicates.late_acquisition_declaration_is_void: The declaration is void and has no effect.

issues.definition: If a land-acquisition declaration falls outside the applicable deadline even after accounting for the actual period of court stay, the declaration is void.
